concept: Rolling resync (initial sync) as a space-reclaim technique on Atlas
summary: Source-anchored research for Rolling resync (initial sync) as a space-reclaim technique on Atlas. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Resyncing a replica-set member is a documented way to reclaim fragmented database-file space after deletions. MongoDB's WiredTiger storage FAQ and Percona's fragmentation advisor both describe this use; the Percona advisor concerns its own monitoring product and does not establish an Atlas procedure. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/faq/storage.md ; https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/advisors/checks/mongodb-collections-fragmented.html

Cisco CPS Operations Guide 24.2.0 explicitly describes member resync as a way to reduce fragmentation and reclaim disk space. Its procedure requires an available primary and stops the target server before clearing its data directory. This is independent evidence for the self-managed mechanism, not authorization or instructions for Atlas. (low confidence)

A self-managed resync destroys the destination member's existing dbPath contents and requires an accessible, up-to-date source. MongoDB warns that resyncing from stale data can undo majority-commit guarantees and cause data loss. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/resync-replica-set-member.md

Inference: a routine Atlas scaling or node-replacement operation must not be advertised as guaranteed defragmentation merely because it performs an initial sync. Atlas may copy a snapshot or files, whereas the logical reclaim rationale depends on rebuilding documents and indexes. Confirm the actual sync method and measure the result before relying on space savings. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/scale-cluster.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync.md

The Cloud Manager rolling-resync recipe cannot be copied verbatim onto Atlas: it waits for rs.stepDown(), and the replSetStepDown command (which rs.stepDown() wraps) is documented as not supported in MongoDB Atlas clusters. This evidence scopes the self-managed recipe; it does not establish whether Atlas Support offers a managed logical-resync workflow. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongocli/current/command/mongocli-cloud-manager-clusters-resync.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replSetStepDown.md

Logical initial sync scans source collections, inserts their documents into new destination collections, builds their indexes in parallel with the copy, and applies buffered oplog changes. Percona documents resyncing a node as one of two ways to reclaim fragmented disk space (the other is compact), and a logical rebuild writes the data afresh rather than preserving the source file layout; the final size is not guaranteed. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync.md ; https://www.percona.com/blog/how-to-reclaim-disk-space-in-percona-server-for-mongodb/

Atlas documents cloud-based initial sync as creating a source-node snapshot and restoring it to a new node. Its scaling documentation says Atlas Core NVMe clusters use file-copy-based initial sync whenever initial sync is required. Both differ from the document-and-index rebuild performed by logical initial sync. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Resyncing a replica-set member can reclaim unused WiredTiger file space that deletions leave available for internal reuse. Percona documents rolling node resync as an alternative to per-collection compaction. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/faq/storage.md ; https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/advisors/checks/mongodb-collections-fragmented.html

Atlas cloud-based initial sync restores a cloud-provider snapshot, whereas logical initial sync scans documents and rebuilds indexes. Therefore, do not assume that an Atlas node replacement or any operation called initial sync will reclaim fragmentation; verify which sync method it uses. This reclaim caution is an inference from the documented mechanisms. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

The documented mongocli rolling-resync commands belong to Cloud Manager and Ops Manager. They resync secondaries, wait for an operator-requested primary stepdown, and then resync the former primary; they remove the contents of each target dbPath. These pages do not establish an Atlas command or Atlas customer access to dbPath. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongocli/current/command/mongocli-cloud-manager-clusters-resync.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongocli/current/command/mongocli-ops-manager-clusters-resync.md

Initial sync needs temporary local-database space for oplog records and a source oplog window long enough to cover synchronization; if a gap in oplog continuity is found, the initial sync restarts from the beginning. A member in STARTUP2 (initial sync) does not participate in write majorities (as of MongoDB 5.0). Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/write-concern.md

Rolling resync is a capacity and availability operation: Percona says it avoids downtime and application impact but can be time consuming for large datasets, and MongoDB documents that initial sync takes longer than subsequent syncs and reduces the performance of the source primary, in a section on NVMe clusters. Sources: https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/advisors/checks/mongodb-collections-fragmented.html ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync.md

The Atlas cluster-modification documentation states that Atlas Core NVMe clusters use file-copy-based initial sync whenever initial sync is required. A tier change on such a cluster should therefore not be presented as a verified logical rebuild for reclaiming fragmentation. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

For self-managed rolling resync, rotate only one member at a time to preserve the write quorum. MongoDB's Cloud Manager CLI documents initial-syncing secondaries in rolling order, waiting for an operator-requested primary stepdown, then initial-syncing the former primary. These are self-managed and Cloud Manager instructions, not evidence of an Atlas resync command. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/resync-replica-set-member.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongocli/current/command/mongocli-cloud-manager-clusters-resync.md

Logical initial sync needs temporary disk space for buffered oplog records in the destination local database and a source oplog window sufficient for catch-up. If catch-up detects an oplog continuity gap, the initial sync must restart from the beginning. (low confidence)

Rolling execution does not guarantee zero application impact. MongoDB warns that initial sync can impact other members and adds traffic to the source member; Atlas warns that migration can affect performance if the primary is already near capacity or if reads go to secondaries. The MongoDB tutorial says initial sync duration depends on database size and network latency. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/resync-replica-set-member.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/scale-cluster.md

MongoDB's Atlas scaling workflow migrates secondaries before the primary, one node at a time per replica set. Its availability guidance recommends retryable writes for primary elections. This supports planning for an election during a managed rolling operation, but does not establish a user-triggered Atlas logical-resync feature. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)
